interactions.summary: Jiang accepts the class move that people give themselves their own weights through free will and then adds a second mechanism: some souls remain burdened because they cannot forgive themselves.

Jiang asks what God is actually doing, receives the answer that God wants people to remove the weights they put on themselves, and sharpens that into a model of God as actively drawing souls toward him.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang question with student answer and reformulation

interactions.summary: A student proposes that God is watching people exercise free will like a spectator, and Jiang immediately tests that image by asking whether God is really just watching.

speaker_notes.note: The diarized label is misleading at the start of the segment: Jiang is speaking first, then a student answers within the same span.

claims.claim: Jiang accepts the idea that people give themselves their own weights in the present through free will, rather than receiving those weights from a judgmental God.
Jiang treats grave sin here not as a divine weight assignment but as the human production of heaviness through one's own choices.
A workable explanation for damnation in this discussion is that some people cannot forgive themselves, or believe they cannot, and so remain stuck under the weights they have created.
claims.temporal_scope: Classroom proposal Jiang accepts as useful on 2026-06-17.

claims.claim: Jiang says God's action is to draw human beings toward him, not to condemn them, and he uses the image of a tractor beam to describe that pull.

signature_moments.moment: The class flips moral weight from something God assigns to something we give ourselves.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's central reversal and keeps the lecture anchored in freedom rather than predestination.

signature_moments.moment: God is figured as a tractor beam already pulling us toward him.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The image compresses Jiang's anti-judgment theology into a memorable picture of attraction rather than surveillance.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: A proposed condition of release from the heaviness people create for themselves; lacking it helps explain why someone remains trapped.
Jiang's metaphor for God's active effort to draw souls toward divine light rather than merely judge them from afar.

chronology_notes.note: This packet moves the discussion from anti-judgment theology into a positive model of attraction, then immediately exposes a new tension between divine drawing and the idea of God as a passive watcher.

uncertainty_notes.note: The movie-watching analogy belongs to a student trial image that Jiang is already beginning to resist, so later reuse should not treat it as Jiang's settled cosmology.
